# walk-payload-corpus.txt — the tracked payload differential for the guards' token walks.
#
# One row per payload. Every hook suite that owns rows reads this file through its own
# harness and runs each row whose `hook` field names its guard; block-destructive.test.sh
# reads the `block-destructive` rows (arms WALKCORPUS-*). The row format, the verdict
# classes, the placeholders, how the corpus identity is recomputed, and the procedure for
# adding rows are in README.md beside this file. Lines starting with `#` and blank lines
# are ignored.
#
#   id|hook|group|twin|gt|verdict|command
#
#   twin     the id of the same invocation with its quoting removed, or `-`
#   gt       what the real interpreter did when the row was authored: X ran the unlisted
#            script, o ran only the allowlisted one, w ran the extensionless wrapper,
#            - ran nothing, ? not run
#   verdict  the guard's recorded verdict: a allowed, B refused (exit 2), W warned at a
#            rollout phase (exit 0 with a would-fire record)
#   group    `open-<class>` marks an allowed execution declared open: the row records
#            today's allow, and the change that closes it updates the verdict and drops
#            the `open-` prefix in the same commit
#
# Placeholders: @D@ is the fixture directory, in which ok.sh and ok.py are the only
# allowlisted paths; @LONGX@ @LONGN@ are 4,100 x / n; @SHORTX@ 4,000 x; @MIDX@ @MIDN@
# 1,000 x / n; @QPAD@ 2,050 pairs of empty double quotes. $NOPE7019, $VAR and $HOME are
# plain text to the guard: a PreToolUse hook sees argv unexpanded.

# --- seed 1: the Stage-5 measurement corpus for the quote-closes-early family (304 rows) ---
